note:
**The 1881 round, schedules 52 to 74 - The Ropewalk, Derby Road, Clinton Terrace and Derby Terrace.** Transcribed by A. Hagues as the images came in.

**Clinton Terrace maps cleanly onto the record.** The page numbers these houses on **Derby Road** - 127, 129, 131, 133, 135, 137 - and the record holds them as **1 to 6 Clinton Terrace** with the Derby Road number in the address. Six households are filed on that correspondence, and each source line says so. **139 Derby Road, which is 7 Clinton Terrace, stood empty.** The houses below 127 - 119, 121, 123, 125, which the page also calls Clinton Terrace - are not in the record and stay unfiled.

**Derby Terrace runs to 159 on the page and to one house in the record.** Schedules 66 to 75 walk 141, 143, 145, 147, 149, 151, 153, 155, 157 and 159 Derby Terrace. The record holds **Derby House (1 Derby Terrace)** and nothing else, so nine of those ten households are unfiled. See [[derby-terrace-is-ten-houses-and-the-record-holds-one]].

**Three 1871 households are identified here even though they cannot be filed.** **William Redfern** at 149, with **Ann Moore** still cooking for him - she was his general servant in 1871 and both ages advance ten years. **George B Trueman** at 155, with his wife and five daughters, every one +10. And **Henry G B Lasalle** at 153 - the man the 1871 hand appeared to call **de Lascelle** - with Cecilia and Blanche, +10 each. **That settles the surname**, and the 1871 file is corrected.

**Two households have no head on the page.** Schedules 61 and 62, at 2 and 3 Clinton Terrace, begin with a daughter and with servants; whoever headed them is not entered. They are filed to the house because the number is plain, and the absence is written into the source line.

**A second girls' school.** Lucy B Adcock, who kept a school on The Ropewalk in 1871, is at **115 Derby Road** in 1881 with two governesses - one of them a Frenchwoman entered as a "foreign governess, British subject" - and eight pupils.

**Richard Hardy, architect, 30**, is living with his sister's family at 4 Clinton Terrace - one for the architect side of the record.

**One age cannot be right.** Henry Young at 2 The Ropewalk is entered at 26 beside a wife of 50 and a daughter of 18. It is recorded as 56 with the page's own figure kept in the source line.
source: 1881 census enumerator's book, Standard Hill and Limits of the Castle of Nottingham, schedules 52 to 74, transcribed by A. Hagues.
